entries.title: Colormap augmentation: a novel method for cross-modality domain generalization.
entries.abstractText:
Purpose

Domain generalization plays a crucial role in analyzing medical images from diverse clinics, scanner vendors, and imaging modalities. Existing methods often require substantial computational resources to train a highly generalized segmentation network, presenting challenges in terms of both availability and cost. The goal of this work is to evaluate a novel, yet simple and effective method for enhancing the generalization of deep learning models in segmentation across varying modalities.

Methods

Eight augmentation methods will be applied individually to a source domain dataset in order to generalize deep learning models. These models will then be tested on completely unseen target domain datasets from a different imaging modality and compared against a lower baseline model. By leveraging standard augmentation techniques, extensive intensity augmentations, and carefully chosen color transformations, we aim to address the domain shift problem, particularly in the cross-modality setting.

Results

Our novel CmapAug method, when combined with standard augmentation techniques, resulted in a substantial improvement in the Dice Score, outperforming the baseline. While the baseline struggled to segment the liver structure in some test cases, our selective combination of augmentation methods achieved Dice scores as high as 83.2%.

Conclusion

Our results highlight the general effectiveness of the tested augmentation methods in addressing domain generalization and mitigating the domain shift problem caused by differences in imaging modalities between the source and target domains. The proposed augmentation strategy offers a simple yet powerful solution to this challenge, with significant potential in clinical scenarios where annotated data from the target domain are limited or unavailable.

entries.title: SET-CNN: Stacked Ensemble of CNNs for Robust Image Embedding and Similarity Retrieval
entries.abstractText: Image retrieval predominantly relies on embedding techniques, which represent visual data as numerical vectors to enable efficient and scalable similarity comparisons. Such embeddings are crucial for a variety of computer vision tasks, including image similarity search, image classification, object detection, and facial recognition. However, conventional techniques that rely on single-network architectures or domain-specific optimizations haveing limited capability to capture the essential and complex visual information required for precise and effective similar image retrieval. To address this limitation, SET-CNN (Stacked Ensemble of CNNs), a novel framework that integrates three diverse pretrained CNN models, DenseNet121, ResNet50, and VGG16 for generating robust image embeddings and enhancing similarity retrieval is proposed. This approach extracts and stacks high-level feature vectors from each base model, concatenates them via feature-level fusion, and processes the unified representation through a meta-model optimized using triplet semi-hard loss to enhance discriminability in the embedding space. Extensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset demonstrate that SET-CNN consistently outperforms individual CNNs and state-of-the-art retrieval methods, achieving a peak training MAP@5 of 0.9286 and a testing MAP@5 of 0.8745, with minimal overfitting. This represents a 7.6% improvement over the best-performing base model. Compared to Deep Semantic Ranking Hashing and Deep Supervised Hashing, SET-CNN delivers absolute gains of +8.6% and +19.9% in MAP@5, respectively, while matching the performance of more complex ResNet attention pooling models without specialized architectural modifications. Embedding quality is assessed through K-Means clustering combined with t-SNE visualization, while final similarity matching is performed using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) with cosine similarity. These clustering and retrieval analyses confirm that the ensemble produces semantically rich and well-separated embeddings, translating into more accurate and relevant retrieval results. Given its performance and flexibility, SET-CNN offers a promising direction for developing generalizable, ensemble-based retrieval systems, with potential extensions to large-scale, multimodal datasets and real-time deployment.

entries.title: Cardio Fusion: A Dual-Stream Regularized Fusion Architecture for Generalizable Cardiovascular Disease Prediction Under Dataset Heterogeneity
entries.abstractText: Computationalrisk-predictionsystems havebecomeanindispensableadjuncttoconventionalclinicaldiagnosis, yet the field continues to be constrained by a persistent methodological obstacle: benchmark datasets remain small, heterogeneous in feature composition, and frequently outdated, while single-classifier models exhibit limited generalizability across diverse patient populations. To address this limitation, the present study proposes a dual-branch hybriddeeplearningarchitecture comprising(i) a tabularbranch,inwhichanL1/L2-regularizeddeepneuralnetworkis ensembled with Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and K-Nearest Neighbour classifiers over a feature subset optimized through Neighbourhood Component Analysis [13], and (ii) an imaging/ECG branch constructed upon ResNet-50 [14], DenseNet-121 [15], and EfficientNet-B0 [16], with the outputs of both branches integrated via a weighted soft-voting meta-learner. The proposed framework is systematically benchmarked across six contemporary datasets, spanning the canonical Cleveland and Statlog repositories, the 920-instance four-hospital combined UCI dataset that has gained prominence in recent (2024–2025) federated learning and interpretability research, a merged 1,190-recordUCI–Kaggle cohort, the feature-rich Z-AlizadehSanicohort[18], andthelongitudinalFraminghamHeart Studycohort [19]. OnthestandardClevelandbenchmark, the proposedregularizedhybridclassifier attains anaccuracy of 96.5%; on a second, independently re-implemented empirical dataset — the 68,612-record Kaggle cardiovascular cohort (cardio_train.csv) — the fused model achieves an accuracy of 73.95% and an AUC-ROC of 80.57% (95% CI: 79.96–81.14), aresult attributabletothe dataset's exclusively lifestyle- and vitals-basedfeature compositionrather than to any deficiency in the proposed architecture. Across the broader multi-dataset benchmark, the framework demonstrates competitive performance relative to recent state-of-the-art systems, including stacked TabNet–XGBoost ensembles (95.20% accuracy, 91.92% F1-score) [2] andappliedartificial-intelligence pipelines reportingaccuracies of up to 99.48% on the Statlog cohort [4]. Collectively, these findings substantiate the premise that the integration of optimized feature selection, architectural hybridization, and explicit regularization yields a classifier that isconcurrently more accurate and more robust across heterogeneous clinical data sources than conventional single-algorithm baselines, thereby reinforcing its viability as a deployable clinical decision-support tool.
